purpose: Five concise source-grounded visual comparison lenses between Heart and Liver; linked to curated original-source anchor IDs, not copied text or scientific validation.

lenses.title: Origins & evolution
lenses.subtitle: The timeline is not the same kind of statement for both organs
lenses.intro: Compare the kinds of evolutionary statements, not just the planetary words.

cards.label: Old Saturn · first disposition
cards.description: Steiner describes a preliminary heart disposition in his Old Saturn account, not a modern physical heart.

cards.label: Earth · recapitulation
cards.description: Another lecture speaks of an early warmth-centered heart configuration while Earth recapitulates previous conditions.

liver.headline: Correspondence, not a proven origin
liver.context: A planetary analogy and a separate elemental relation

cards.label: Jupiter · inner analogy
cards.description: GA 128 offers a provisional Jupiter correspondence. It does not date anatomical liver formation to the planet Jupiter.

cards.label: Water · elemental relation
cards.description: GA 205 associates the liver with the water element in a different spiritual context.

lenses.distinction: Old Saturn as a cosmic stage, Earth recapitulation, Jupiter as an inner analogy and the water element are four different predicates. There is no valid single organ-builder timeline to infer from them.

lenses.title: In the organism
lenses.subtitle: How each organ is discussed in the living body
lenses.intro: The source-linked medical lectures emphasize different systems and relations.

cards.label: Rhythm
cards.description: GA 313 discusses rhythmic activity in relation to influences of the head and metabolic organization.

cards.label: Heart–lung relation
cards.description: The 1922 medical discussion connects heart and lung organization with an etheric account.

cards.label: Nourishment
cards.description: GA 128 discusses the liver alongside bile and spleen in nutritive processes.

cards.label: Liver–gall
cards.description: GA 314 relates the liver–gall organization to warmth/I processes. This broader system must not be treated as liver-only.

lenses.distinction: These are Steiner's historical interpretations of organismic activity, not established explanations replacing cardiovascular or metabolic physiology.

lenses.title: Inner life & will
lenses.subtitle: Purported spiritual perception and human experience
lenses.intro: The most striking ideas are not claims of the same type.

cards.label: Inner perception
cards.description: GA 316 characterizes the heart as a purported inward sense of astral and I-related activity.

cards.label: Conscience
cards.description: GA 205 connects aspects of the heart with conscience and future-life spiritual imagery.

cards.label: Food value
cards.description: GA 316 portrays the liver as a purported inward sense for the value of nourishment.

cards.label: Intention into action
cards.description: GA 317 proposes that liver organization participates in a child's will-to-movement process.

lenses.distinction: Spiritual inward-sense images and child-development assertions must be read as attributed esoteric positions; they are not clinical measurements or diagnoses.

lenses.title: Who is said to act?
lenses.subtitle: Named beings, human members and the limits of claims
lenses.intro: The Atlas separates spiritual actors from organs, analogies and human constituent members.

heart.headline: Early cosmic beings ≠ exclusive modern-heart builder

cards.label: Old Saturn context
cards.description: GA 110 discusses hierarchical activity around early cosmic development; it does not give a simple exclusive modern-heart builder chart.

cards.label: Present human organization
cards.description: GA 316 refers to astral and I processes in an inner-sense interpretation, not a separately named hierarchy.

liver.headline: No sole hierarchy established in this selected set

cards.label: Jupiter ≠ a hierarchy
cards.description: The inner-Jupiter analogy in GA 128 does not identify a single spiritual hierarchy making the liver.

cards.label: I in liver–gall
cards.description: GA 314 refers to the human I organization in a liver–gall relationship; the I is not a separate angelic rank.

lenses.distinction: Do not infer an exclusive hierarchy for either organ merely from a planetary, elemental or human-member correspondence.

lenses.title: Unresolved questions
lenses.subtitle: What the current evidence does not yet settle
lenses.intro: A useful Atlas makes research gaps visible without turning them into definitive answers.

cards.label: Chronology and hierarchy
cards.description: How exactly do Old Saturn agency statements relate to later Earth recapitulation, once every passage and German text is compared?

cards.label: Medical error
cards.description: Steiner denied that the heart pumps blood in GA 205. Established physiology demonstrates that it does pump blood.

cards.label: Liver vs liver–gall
cards.description: Which claims explicitly concern the liver alone, and which concern a wider liver–gall organization?

cards.label: Clinical validity
cards.description: Claims relating liver activity to childhood will or disability do not constitute evidence-based neurological explanations.

lenses.distinction: Neither the visual guide nor a first English passage audit is independent confirmation of anthroposophical medicine, cosmic organ evolution or complete German-text reconciliation.
